sourceEvidence.finding: AuthorWorkspace owns workRef, React work publication, navigation and scene-load epochs, generation, author scope, strict journal queue, and draft timers.

Text edits update authoritative workRef and construct the operation before delayed React publication; draft writes remain on the existing 350 ms timer. Moving the code does not remove these operations.

Scene loads bind navigation, scene request, author, repository, and snapshot freshness across composition flush, strict draft flush, remote reads, receipt/journal reads, live-generation reconciliation, and final publication.

Writes are serialized and completion is applied only to the matching navigation, author, entry, and text; flush loops until the live text is recoverable. The journal uses a strict transaction and awaits transaction completion.
putLatestDraft validates the operation, opens a strict read/write IndexedDB transaction, rejects newer/equal-generation conflicts, replaces only older same-author drafts, and awaits completion.
Restore drains pending writes and checks captured repository/document/scene/author plus operation ID/generation before replacement; a changed draft is retained or re-persisted.
Restore removes only draft records for the same repository, document, and author using a strict write transaction; checkpointed and protected entries are not selected.

sourceEvidence.finding: Reading, history, input, preview, and typography modules are statically imported; the component owns editor pending-text state and composition-flush registration.
Resume position restoration and print both interact with the live editor instance and its flush/focus lifecycle.

Reading and inline history have conditional mount paths; the editor remains mounted in hidden columns during reading, while preview, scratch, print, and history behavior share the scene's current text and identity.
The SceneEditor instance is keyed by author scope, repository, document path, and write permission and receives the current resume, history, text, durability, and navigation contracts.
Workspace invokes the selected panel render; moving history into another component does not require unmounting the editor.
Contribution modules use a separate generated loader and selected-instance abort/dispose lifecycle; C11 does not need to restructure that path.
